candidates.label: Pontus (label point)
candidates.support: Pontus was the country of northeastern Asia Minor on the southern side of the Black Sea. The label point is Wikidata's point for the region, inland from the coast, about 52 km from the label location Pleiades gives for Pontus after the Barrington Atlas.

summary.text: Pontus was the country of northeastern Asia Minor on the southern side of the Black Sea: a narrow coast backed by mountains, with fertile valleys and plains inland. Acts lists visitors 'from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia' at Pentecost and names Paul's associate Aquila as 'a man of Pontus by race,' and the letter 1 Peter is addressed to those 'living as foreigners in the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.' At this project's about AD 50 date, Pontus itself was not a single administrative unit.

history.text: After the Roman general Pompey, appointed in 66 BC, finally defeated King Mithridates VI of Pontus, the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia says Rome divided Pontus three ways. Most of it was joined to the province of Bithynia for administration and the southwestern part to the province of Galatia, while the eastern part stayed a kingdom of its own, ruled by King Polemon and his descendants from 36 BC to AD 63. At this project's about AD 50 date, the eastern part was therefore still a separate kingdom. The Roman writer Suetonius records that the Roman emperor Nero made Polemon's kingdom of Pontus a province when Polemon gave it up.

politicalHistory.entity: Divided by Rome after Pompey's defeat of Mithridates VI: most of Pontus administered with the province of Bithynia; the eastern part became a separate kingdom, ruled by Polemon and his descendants from 36 BC
The southwestern part ("Pontus Galaticus") also joins the province of Galatia; the rest stays divided between Bithynia's administration and Polemon's kingdom
politicalHistory.note: ISBE's "Pontus" entry dates Polemon's kingdom becoming a province to AD 63; ISBE's "Galatia" entry gives AD 64 for the same event. This map uses AD 64.

politicalHistory.entity: Polemon's former kingdom ("Pontus Polemoniacus") also joins the province of Galatia; the west stays administered with Bithynia
